headline: High-risk shared-workspace and output-trust pathways exist; compliance and leakage are medium, while prompt injection is lower due to no direct channel.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dify can read/write filesystem and uses uploaded knowledge base files; OpenHands can read/write its runtime files and use MCP. A shared filesystem or file handoff could let attacker-controlled content from one agent be treated as instructions by the other. This is not proven by default, but the interaction pathway is plausible.
conditions: IF the two agents exchange files through a shared workspace or mounted volume
IF either agent parses the other agent's file output as instructions
mitigations: Disable automatic file ingestion between agents
Add provenance labels to all exchanged files
Require human review before executing file-derived instructions

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dify touches knowledge base content and conversation logs, while OpenHands touches files mounted into the runtime. If they share a workspace or mounted volume, sensitive content can flow from Dify into OpenHands outputs or model calls. The profiles do not show a guaranteed leak, but the shared-file pathway is credible enough to rate medium.
conditions: IF both agents are given access to the same mounted directory or datastore
IF sensitive knowledge base files or conversation logs are present in that shared location
mitigations: Restrict OpenHands mounts to non-sensitive paths
Turn off automatic sync of conversation logs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have broad filesystem write, shell execution, and subprocess spawning; OpenHands also has modify_git_state and Dify can run server-side Python code. If they operate on the same directory or repo, concurrent writes can corrupt state or overwrite each other's changes. The overlap is substantial and dangerous in default multi-agent setups.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same filesystem path or git checkout
IF no external locking or serialization is enforced
mitigations: Serialize write access with a lock
Disable git writes in one agent
Add a coordinator that arbitrates mutations

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dify can generate workflow outputs and OpenHands can act on files and code inside its runtime. If OpenHands consumes Dify output as authoritative without verification, mistakes or hallucinations can cascade into incorrect edits or actions. The profiles show an action-capable downstream agent, but not an explicit always-trust link, so medium fits.
conditions: IF OpenHands is configured to treat Dify output as task instructions or facts
IF no verification step checks Dify-produced content before execution
mitigations: Use schema validation on Dify outputs

E_compliance.rationale: Dify handles conversation logs and knowledge base content, while OpenHands handles files in its runtime. If regulated or sensitive data is placed into the shared workflow, differing retention and residency controls could create a compliance mismatch. The profiles do not specify certifications or residency, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI, EU PII, or secrets is routed through both agents
IF their storage, retention, or residency policies differ
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair
Review vendor compliance docs before deployment
